C. Significant Impact on Air Quality
The air quality impact of this project has been analyzed by the Illinois Department of Transportation, Bureau of Environmental Science, for ambient quality and for the 1-hour and 8-hour maximum traffic considerations. The air quality impact of the carbon monixide concentrations are not considered to be a severe impact since they are below the standards established by the Federal Environmental Protection Agency and those of the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency. Air pollution resulting from this project was determined to not be significant based on guidance obtained from Illinois Environmental Protections Agency, and in accordance with proposed FHWA PPM 90-7 relating to precoordination and review procedures.
D. Use of Section 4(f) Lands
The State of Illinois Department of Transportation will require the temporary use of less than 0.2 acres of land for the removal of wingwalls from the bridge over Thorn Creek and to provide a safer grade for the entrance driveway into the Cook County Forest Preserve District site, located in the northwest quadrant of the intersection between Lincoln Highway and Chicago Road.
E. Acquisition of Roosevelt School Property
Frontage land from Roosevelt School in the City of Chicago Heights will be required for right-of-way purposes to accomplish the highway widening and reconstruction. After replacing as much contiguous land as feasible to the school site, there will be a resulting irreversible commitment of 4,385 square feet (0.10 acres) of open space land to highway purposes.
F. Drainage
Surface run-off is critical at valley edges where water from large areas collect and enter the more positive run-off and catchment system of a stream bed or river. Alteration could cause erosive concentrations from run-off or could divert quantities of water from critical ground water recharge areas.
Drainage for this proposed improvement will be in accordance with the provisions and limitations established by the General Assembly of the State of Illinois, as contained in the Illinois Revised Statutes. Present watershed drainage patterns will be maintained and every effort will be made to avoid implicating any water supply source, treatment or distribution system.
